summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Meridian security and platform stakeholders through what admin and privileged activity is captured, how audit exports can be configured (S3, Kafka, Splunk HEC, webhook, syslog), and options for retention and encryption (CMEK/HSM). Customer asked for sample configs and a short POC to stream audit events to their Splunk instance; follow-ups include sharing an architecture diagram, running a 24-hour export test, and aligning on retention/compliance requirements.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-12-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Sofia Alvarez (Redwood AE), Michael Chen (Redwood SE), Janelle Ortiz (CSM); Aisha Khan (Meridian Head of Security), Liam O'Connell (Platform), Priya Menon (Compliance), Derek Yu (SRE)

00:00 - Sofia: hey everyone thanks for carving out time, we've got about an hour. this is Sofia from Redwood, joined by Michael our SE and Janelle from CSM. how are you all?
00:10 - Aisha: good thanks, excited to dig in on audit capture and how we can meet our evidence requirements for SOC 2 and internal audits.
00:20 - Michael: great, quick agenda I'll outline what events we capture today, export destinations, retention controls, and encryption options then we'll tune to your specific needs. feel free to interrupt.
00:35 - Liam: yes please, we mostly care about privileged activity — console/admin actions, API keys usage, role changes, and any data access events tied to PII. also curious about near realtime streaming to our SIEM.
00:50 - Michael: absolutely. at a high level Redwood captures admin events (user creation, role grants, permission changes), token/key lifecycle events, model route changes, deployment rollouts, and API tokens usage. on the data side we capture request metadata (requestor id, route, model version) but not full prompt content unless you enable application traces — default is metadata only for evidence.
01:10 - Priya: metadata only ok for a lot of audit cases, but for legal discovery we may need some payloads for flagged sessions. can that be toggled?
01:20 - Michael: yes, we have a configurable trace flag — you can enable request capture for specified routes or users. note that enabling full request payload capture increases retention and storage costs and also has privacy implications. we'll show filters so you only capture what you need.
01:40 - Derek: how is that data exported? we want an architecture that pushes events to our Splunk HEC and also archives to an S3 bucket in eu-west-1.
01:50 - Michael: export options: batch exports to S3 (parquet/json), streaming via Kafka or nabla-topic, webhook push, syslog for onprem SIEMs, and direct Splunk HEC integration. for S3 you can choose partitioning by date/service and lifecycle rules to tier to glacier. for Splunk we stream in near-realtime via HEC tokens.
02:15 - Aisha: any out-of-the-box schema? we need specific fields for forensic queries.
02:22 - Sofia: yes we have a documented schema: timestamp, event_type, actor_id, actor_role, resource_type, resource_id, action, result_status, request_id, region, model_version, route_path, and optional trace_payload. i'll share the doc after the call.
02:40 - Liam: what's the default retention?
02:45 - Michael: default hosted retention is 90 days for admin/audit by default. enterprise plans can extend to multi-year retention and we support archiving to customer-owned S3 for indefinite retention. in private deployments you control retention fully.
03:05 - Priya: how does this map to SOC 2 evidence? we need chain-of-custody, tamper-evidence, and key management proof.
03:15 - Michael: for SOC 2: we provide append-only logs with integrity checks, exportable evidence bundles and audit trails for admin actions. encryption at rest uses service-managed keys by default, and we support CMEK (customer-managed keys) backed by KMS or HSM for extra control. key rotation logs are captured as events too.
03:35 - Aisha: KMS — do you support AWS CMKs and external HSMs?
03:40 - Michael: yes to both. AWS KMS CMKs are supported for hosted exports; for Private we support on-prem HSM integrations and bring-your-own-key via external KMS APIs. sometimes the transcript shows KMS as K-M-S-E, sorry the auto-transcript.
03:55 - Derek: if we export to our S3, do we maintain immutability / object lock for compliance?
04:00 - Michael: good question. Redwood can write to a customer-owned S3 bucket and we recommend enabling Object Lock/Write Once Read Many (WORM) with legal hold for retention. Redwood will not overwrite objects once written during the export flow.
04:18 - Priya: about RBAC — do you capture policy changes and grant revocations?
04:22 - Michael: yes, RBAC events are captured. we record the before/after for role changes and include actor metadata. note that in transcripting sometimes R-back gets mis-typed, sorry.
04:35 - Liam: curious about latencies for streaming to Splunk; we have an SLA around forensics under two minutes.
04:45 - Michael: Splunk HEC pipeline typically delivers sub-30s in our tests for steady state. for bursts we have buffering and backpressure, and you can choose guaranteed delivery via Kafka connectors with at-least-once semantics. we'll include a performance note in the export doc.
05:10 - Aisha: are there built-in retention policies or must we manage lifecycle on our side?
05:20 - Michael: both. Redwood enforces platform retention by default. you can also configure push exports to your archive where you control S3 lifecycle. for e-discovery we often recommend a two-tier approach: hot logs (90 days) in Redwood for quick queries, archive older logs in S3 with indices retained in your SIEM.
05:45 - Sofia: does anyone want to see a quick config example? I can share a sample S3 export policy and Splunk HEC setup after the call.
05:55 - Priya: yes please. also we need to know how you prove log integrity for auditors — hashes?
06:10 - Michael: we include SHA256 checksums on export files and maintain an export manifest with checksums and timestamps. these manifests are versioned and can be exported as evidence bundles.
06:30 - Derek: about cross-region residency — our data residency rules require EU-only storage for certain tenant scopes. can you do region-scoped exports?
06:40 - Michael: yes, exports can be targeted to region-specific buckets and we have VPC endpoints for EU regions. Private deployments let you ensure no egress from your region.
06:55 - Liam: any known gaps we should be aware of?
07:05 - Michael: current gaps: very large payload capture at scale needs planning due to storage, and some legacy connectors to older SIEMs may need a small adaptor. for on-prem air-gapped environments there is an additional appliance-based export we'll walk through.
07:30 - Aisha: can we request an event-level contract for retention and export SLAs?
07:38 - Sofia: yes that's typically part of enterprise discussions — we can add export availability & retention SLAs to the contract. i'll flag that to our sales ops.
07:50 - Priya: question on user deletion — if a user is removed, do their historical events get anonymized or kept?
08:00 - Michael: historical events are retained as-is for audit integrity. we can pseudonymize or redact PII fields for privacy but the event skeleton remains for chain-of-custody.
08:20 - Derek: show me how a Splunk HEC payload looks — is the event structured or plain text?
08:30 - Michael: structured JSON. here's an example we pasted in the doc: {timestamp, event_type, actor:{id, email, role}, action, resource, metadata, trace_id}. i'll send full examples.
08:55 - Liam: how are API key rotations logged? we need clear evidence that a key was rotated and old key invalidated.
09:05 - Michael: key rotation is an event type; we log both start and completion along with actor and request IDs. if you use CMEK, key rotation ops are also recorded in the KMS audit.
09:25 - Aisha: can we integrate with our central KMS for key material for exports?
09:30 - Michael: yes for hosted S3 exports you can use AWS CMKs; for more advanced HSM integrations we support via customer-managed connectors in Private mode.
09:45 - Priya: legal will want a mapping doc between Redwood events and SOC 2 control IDs.
09:50 - Sofia: we have a SOC 2 evidence mapping, i'll attach it. it maps event types to control objectives (CC6, CC7 equivalents).
10:05 - Derek: how do you handle deletions or retention requests under GDPR?
10:12 - Michael: data subject requests are supported; if a deletion request applies to user-identifiable traces we can redact or pseudonymize while preserving the event id for audit, process logged and time-stamped. we will coordinate with your privacy team.
10:30 - Aisha: any differences between Hosted, Dedicated, Private around audit fidelity?
10:35 - Michael: fidelity is comparable; Private gives you full control of export endpoints and keys. Dedicated (reserved capacity) still uses Redwood-managed export pipelines but can be configured to push to your targets with CMEK.
10:55 - Liam: can we run a short POC to validate Splunk HEC ingestion, schema, and latency?
11:00 - Sofia: yes, Michael suggested a 24-hour POC to stream audit events into your Splunk test index and a concurrent S3 dump for archival. we'll provide credentials and sample configs.
11:12 - Priya: timeline — we aim to have this validated before our audit window in late Jan. sound OK?
11:20 - Sofia: absolutely. we can target finishing the POC by mid-December so you have time for legal review.
11:30 - Aisha: are there examples of other finance customers who have done long-term retention with S3 object lock?
11:36 - Michael: yes a few of our banking customers use our S3 export + object lock pattern for regulatory retention. i'll anonymize and share their architecture notes.
11:50 - Derek: any potential costs we should flag? storage, egress, and Splunk ingestion fees come to mind.
11:58 - Sofia: we'll provide a cost estimate sheet — storage, streaming egress, and optional retained search indexes. also note that longer retention on our platform adds per-GB charges unless archived to customer-owned S3.
12:15 - Priya: excellent. let's recap next steps.
12:20 - Sofia: recap: we'll send export schema, sample configs for S3+Splunk, run a 24-hour POC streaming to Meridian test Splunk HEC and S3, provide SOC 2 mapping doc and evidence pack. action items assigned in the notes.
12:35 - Aisha: thanks all, this was helpful. looking forward to docs and the POC.
12:45 - Sofia: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs. end call.

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., R-back for RBAC, sock two for SOC 2) and some speaker attribution jitter from auto-transcribe.
